title: Linux Fundamentals Workshop
subtitle: From double-click to the shell: files, permissions, pipes, and a terminal you are not afraid of.
description: A hands-on session for first-years who have never opened a terminal. Attendees work on live systems with a mentor per table, covering navigation, permissions, pipes, redirection, and a real (small) task: fixing a deliberately broken configuration.
register: Notify the club page — seats are limited to 24.

title: Intro to Git & Open Source
subtitle: Your first pull request, without the fear: branching, rebasing, and reading a real codebase.
description: A practical introduction to version control for students stuck in the 'zip file' era. We clone a small real repository, break it, fix it, and submit a practice pull request against a club repo with review feedback from senior members.
register: Bring a laptop with Git installed.

title: Build Week — First Hackathon
subtitle: 48 hours, one real problem, real tools. The goal is shipped, not slides.
description: Our first 48-hour build event. Teams pick a problem from a provided list (or their own), use the club's stack guides, and must deliver something runnable by Sunday noon. Mentors from all study groups float between teams. Judging is 40% working software, 40% engineering judgment, 20% documentation.

title: Networking Deep Dive Series
subtitle: A five-week series from ARP to TLS, using tcpdump as the only visual aid.
description: A slow, weekly walk through the network stack built on the CampusMesh experiment. Each session observes one protocol layer with real packets. No slides full of boxes — every claim is checked against a capture.

title: Orientation — Semester Opening
subtitle: What the club is, how it runs, and the three study groups that were opening that week.
description: The semester-opening orientation. Existing members ran short lightning talks on the reading groups, demoed three projects, and explained how a new member goes from zero to first contribution.

title: First Code Night
subtitle: An evening of silent, shared work: bring a problem, leave with a commit.
description: The first of our quiet working nights. No talks, no schedule — just the lab, tea, mentors, and four hours to make progress on whatever you brought. Twelve commits landed.

title: CTF: Beginner Track
subtitle: A gentle, self-hosted capture-the-flag: crypto, web, reversing, and one bash puzzle.
description: A low-stakes CTF built and hosted by club members on college infrastructure. Twenty-one teams solved at least one flag; the beginner web challenge had the most solvers, and the final bash puzzle stumped everyone for an hour.
